In summary, our research is concerned with
a new compound of a S = 3 / 2 ion, Co(2+).
a new Co(2+) compound with a tetrahedral geometry, which has a spin S = 3 ground state and a magnetic ground state without orbital degeneracy.
the synthesis and characterization of a Co(2+)-containing compound, (C(4)H(12)N(2))[CoCl(4)], based upon a tetrahalometallate anion and an organic cation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tetrahedral CoCl4(2-) anion, as found in the compound (C4H 12N2) [CoCl4], is a rare example of a Co(2+) compound with a spin S = 3 / 2 ground state and no spin-orbit coupling.
the orbital degeneracies are lifted by a tetrahedral ligand field in the case of the compound (C4H10N2)[CoX4] (X = Cl, Br) and the spin-orbit coupling remains negligible.
the Co(2+) ion in the tetrahedral compound is in a spin-only S = 3 / 2 state with an effective g-factor close to 2.0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic behavior of Co(2+) is highly dependent on the local environment.
the magnetic properties of Co(2+) in a tetrahedral environment is highly sensitive to small changes in ligand environment.
the tetrahedral coordination environment for Co(2+) is unique in that it does not show the orbital degeneracies that are found for the octahedral and other tetrahedral Co compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic properties of Co(2+) can depend on subtle differences in the local environment.
the tetrahedral CoCl4 environment is not sufficient to induce a spin-orbit coupling.
the tetrahedral coordination of Co(2+) can lead to a S = 3 spin ground state in the absence of spin-orbital coupling.
